newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Spector to raise capital by 2.75 bln Bfr.
newsitem.headline: Spector to raise capital by 2.75 bln Bfr.

text.p: Belgian photo processing group Spector NV said on Tuesday it had fixed its planned capital increase at 2.75 billion Belgian francs, above a two-billion- franc estimate initially given to investors.
Spector said on September 6 it would raise its capital and issue a convertible bond to help pay for a restructuring of the group and acquisitions.
The planned convertible bond issue has now been scrapped, the company said in its statement on Tuesday.

The restructuring will leave Swiss photo finishing group Porst Holding AG with a 50.2 percent stake in Spector, which in turn will control Porst's operational units, including Belgian electrical goods retailer Photo Hall.
Spector said Porst would subscribe to the capital increase for the full 50.2 percent.

Investors who bought into the group's May 1995 convertible bond issue would have the right to exercise early the bond's warrants to take part in the capital increase. Conditions would be announced later, Spector said.
